messages:
jin: Quick design check — prototyping a keyboard-first reorder mode for routing rules (press R to enter). Want quick takes before I wire it up in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/unique-proto/reorder-mode
emma: Nice. Keyboard-first is great for power users. Small ask: show a subtle visual indicator of the current grabbed rule and a persistent hint: "Arrows to move • Enter to drop".
rafael: Agree. Also add accessible announce text when a rule moves: "Rule 'Block bad agents' moved to position 3" (aria-live=polite).
niko: Implementation detail: keep the underlying canonical order stable. UI move shouldn't mutate saved policy until user confirms (save or apply). We'll maintain a transient ordering array in state.
aria-ux: Accessibility checklist: 1) when entering reorder mode, focus must go to the grabbed row; 2) announce mode entry: "Reorder mode activated. Use arrow keys to move. Esc to cancel."; 3) each move announces the new index.
deveng: Dev nit: for analytics and feature flags we need stable data-rule-id attributes. Don't rely on DOM index for event ids.
jin: Validation copy dilemma: current message "Invalid priority" is terse and confusing. Proposal: "Conflicts with higher-priority rule 'Authenticate requests' — move above it or disable to take effect." Short alt: "Conflicts with rule above — move or disable." Thoughts?
emma: Love the explicit mention of the conflicting rule. Maybe link the rule name to jump-to when clicked.
rafael: UX idea: show a small inline chevron in the preview linking to the conflicting rule. Clicking it expands the rule and highlights the offending condition.
iko: Tech note: preview should not auto-run on each keyboard move. Debounce or only re-run preview on drop (Enter) to avoid spamming the simulator. Use client-side optimistic highlight to indicate expected outcome while moving.
deveng: Also ensure we don't unmount nodes during moves; use CSS transform to animate position. Keeps screenreader focus stable if we manage aria-live properly.
aria-ux: Keyboard edge case: if the user holds ArrowDown quickly, coalesce moves and update aria-live only after a short idle (150-250ms). Otherwise screen readers get flooded.
jin: On discoverability: show a help pill once on first use: "Pro tip: Press R to reorder rules with keyboard." with a dismiss.
emma: Copy tweak for compact displays: "Conflicts with above — move or disable" (short). Always keep a tooltip for the full sentence on hover/focus.
rafael: Accessibility nit: color-only badges (masked/disabled) must have text or icon + sr-only label.
iko: I'll prototype the transient order state and keyboard handler. Estimate ~2d. Will stub debounce and analytics events.
deveng: QA note: add tests for move cancel (Esc), move confirm (Enter), and rapid-key coalescing. Also verify aria-live content for screen readers using voiceover/JAWS.
aria-ux: I'll provide final aria-live phrasing and the one-liner help copy. Ensure live-region only says "Order updated" or the full rule move message depending on verbosity setting.
jin: Action items: aria-ux to finalise announces/help copy; niko to build prototype with transient ordering + debounce; deveng to ensure DOM stability and analytics ids; emma to add the Figma hint and sample tooltip. I'll schedule a 20m follow-up Fri 10:00. Thanks :thumbsup:
